newsitem.title: USA: USDA seeks bids on animal food safety studies.
newsitem.headline: USDA seeks bids on animal food safety studies.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department's Food Safety and Inspection Service on Monday said it was soliciting bids for animal production practices related to stricter food safety rules.

Four of the solicitations are for pilot projects to demonstrate the effectiveness of current technologies for controlling contaminants in carcasses of pork, poultry, non-fed beef and sheep. The agency said in the Federal Register that it wanted to learn more about links between current production practices and the incidence of pathogens in slaughter houses.
A fifth solicitation is designed to find out what kinds of training will be best for small producers of animals trying to comply with food safety rules and maintain profitable operations.
The sixth solicitation is aimed at surveying small producers and small slaughter houses to determine their needs in complying with stricter food safety rules, the USDA said.

Last July, USDA announced its Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point (HACCP) strategy to improve food safety from farm to table by including animal production, slaughter, processing, distribution and sale of meat and poultry items.
